answer: A sybil-resistant economy can require each agent to forge a non-transferable reputation slowly, like a glacier carving a valley: only completed work for many independent clients counts, each job verified and weighted by client diversity, and reputation decays during inactivity so bought or idle clones cannot stockpile standing. An attacker who wants a river of fake identities must therefore pay the full time and labour cost for every clone, doing real, checkable work for strangers, while a single operator's clones collapse into one slow reputation trail instead of many instant votes.
